summary: Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held posts at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and the University of Calcutta, where he was attested as Professor in 2009. He also taught Kuntala Bhattacharya.
Prabhasa Dharma (1931–1999) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teachers Seikaku Hirata and Joshu Sasaki, the latter in 1967.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi (1898–1956) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology scholar. He earned degrees at the University of Calcutta and University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi, later holding professorships at Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati University.
Pragati Sahni specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. A former student of Damien Keown, she was attested as an Associate Professor at the University of Delhi in 2026.
Praggnaparamita Biswas works in Indology. Supervised for doctoral studies by Ratna Basu, she was attested as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Prahlad Pradhan (1910–1982) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Patna University and Visva-Bharati University. His career included posts at Visva-Bharati, Ravenshaw College, Gangadhar Meher University as Principal, and Utkal University as Professor (~1968–1976).

Pramod Chandra (1930–2016) was an art historian and Indologist. After studies at Elphinstone College, Georgetown, and the University of Mumbai, he held posts at CSMVS (~1954–1962), the University of Chicago (1971–1980), and Harvard University (1980–2004).

Prasanna Venkatesh T S works in computational fields and Indology. He has held positions at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College as a Ph.D. Research Scholar and at the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad.
Prasarn Lao-areun specializes in philosophy and Indology. He studied under Viroj Inthanon and earned a PhD from the University of Mysore (attested 2014).

Pratap Chandra Chunder (1919–2008) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Hindu School, Presidency University (~1936–1940), and the University of Calcutta, where he studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.

Pratapaditya Pal (born 1935) is an Indology, Tibetology, and art history scholar. He earned doctorates from the University of Calcutta and University of Cambridge, later serving as curator at the MFA Boston, LACMA, and the Art Institute of Chicago.

Prayag Raj Sharma (born 1939) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Dean at CNAS (attested 1973), Professor at Tribhuvan University (attested 1976–1990), and was on the advisory editorial board of Kailash (attested 1976).

Prayoon Mererk (born 1955) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi in 1985 under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

id: P:Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
summary: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark (1908–1980) was a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Lycée Janson-de-Sailly and the London School of Economics (~1935–1939), and served in the Office of Strategic Services (~1944–1945).

Priyanku Chakraborty specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Aishwarya Biswas, Chakraborty held an appointment as Rajendralal Mitra Research Fellow in Buddhist Studies at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Priyavrat Sharma (1920–2008) was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Director at Banaras Hindu University and its Postgraduate Institute of Indian Medicine.

Prods Oktor Skjærvø (born 1944) specializes in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. After degrees from Oslo and Mainz, he served at Mainz (1980–1985), Columbia University (1984–1991), and Harvard University as Aga Khan Professor (~1991–2015).
Przemysław Szczurek is an Indologist. He has held positions at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań and at the University of Breslau, where he was attested as Professor of Indology in 2021.

Pulinbihari Chakravarti worked in Indology and philosophy, having studied under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at The Asiatic Society (attested 1951).
Punyavijaya (1895–1971) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He founded the Prakrit Text Society.
